subject: Re: Error in prettyDate: range too small for min.n

messages.author: c1c18b994acde272
messages.subject: Re: Error in prettyDate: range too small for min.n
parts:
Update: I've worked around this problem by plotting an offset, in microseconds, from the minimum range. However, it would be great to know whether if ggplot can be configured to handle nanosecond precision as I like how well it currently deals with dates and would be a shame to not use R's native Date Time types.

Albert

On Tuesday, 8 January 2013 17:05:23 UTC+11, Albert wrote:
Hello There,

Below is a very basic example of how to reproduce the "range too small for min.n" error message and I've attached the sample data file:

> tmp_data<-read.csv("tmp_data.csv")
> tmp_data_trans<-transform(tmp_data, TIME=as.POSIXct(strptime(TIME, format="%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%OS")))
> tmp_data
  CUMULATIVE_VOLUME                             TIME
1                 0 2012/12/13 11:00:00.150732821000
2               476 2012/12/13 11:00:00.152731900000
> ggplot(tmp_data_trans, aes(x=TIME, y=CUMULATIVE_VOLUME)) + geom_line()
Error in prettyDate(x = x, n = n, min.n = min.n, sep = sep, ...) :
  range too small for min.n

Does anyone know how to get around this issue? I tried "hacking" in an additional row at the top which appeared to prevent the error:

0,2012/12/13 10:59:58.150732821000

But clearly, this is not an acceptable solution. I'd just like to be able to plot down to a nanosecond precision.

Thanks all!
Albert
